# Review — iliad-080 (Iliad 13.266–360)

Reviewer pass on `units.json` (pass 1), then `gloss.json` and a re-check of the units (pass 2). `t` was never touched (checked: every unit's `t` is identical to the drafter's, and the units still tile the 95 lines). `new-renderings.md` was updated to match every changed rendering.

Severity: **major** = a house rendering the tables fix was not followed, or the English/Greek reading was wrong; **medium** = a false grammatical or factual claim in a note or entry, or an open sense presented as settled; **minor** = polish, consistency of a note with the renderings, wording.

## How the conventions were checked

`conventions.md` (Iliad) front matter and rules, and the Odyssey conventions' rules (verse, two English layers, Homeric flags, glossary entries, notes, scansion), were read in full. The two house-renderings tables (about 4,300 and 1,150 rows) were not read top to bottom; instead every word-form of the 95 lines was matched by script against the first cell of every row of both tables (exact form, 7-letter stem, and a second pass on forty-odd stems such as ἀμύν-, ἐρίζ-, νεμεσ-, στέρν-, βέλ-, κήρ-, χερμάδ-), and every row that matched was read. The deviations below all came out of that. Neighbouring text: the last units of iliad-079 (the speech this part answers, its mention of the spears standing in Idomeneus’ hut at 260–261, and the published lines at 254) and the published units behind every repeated line (iliad-023, -068, -077) were read. No translation was opened or recalled.

## Findings considered and refused

- **268 `i` “not near enough to take”**: the “enough” is not in the Greek. Kept: οὐ σχεδόν ἐστιν ἑλέσθαι is “it is not near, to take (them)”, and “not near enough to take” says the same in English; the force is unchanged.
- **302 `i` “arm themselves for the Ephyri”**: “for” is ambiguous between “against” and “on behalf of”. Kept: μέτα + accusative is itself open (“toward, among, in quest of”) and the next lines say they heed neither side; `l` keeps “toward”.
- **312 ἀμύνειν “to defend” against the table’s ἀμύνω “ward off”**: the table’s “ward off” is for ἀμύνω with the thing warded off in the accusative (λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι); here the ships are in the dative and nothing is warded off by name. Kept “defend”; the glosser recorded the absolute use. (ἀλέξω is also “defend” in the tables, 1.590 and 5.779; the two are five lines apart in this part but are different verbs in different speeches, and the table fixes both.)
- **325 `i` “in speed of foot”**: reads the dative ποσί as speed, which the Greek leaves implicit. Kept: the unit note says the contrast is running, “in a footrace” (named as avoided in new-renderings) would add a race, and the draft’s phrase adds nothing else.
- **340 `i` “spears that cut the skin” against the table’s “skin-cutting” (4.510–511)**: the table’s `i` is for the attributive use with “bronze”; here ταμεσίχροας is a predicate adjective on the spears. `l` keeps “skin-cutting” exactly. Kept.
- **289 αὐχέν’ case**: accusative or dative (ἐν αὐχέν’ ~ ἐνὶ νώτῳ) is not decided by the form; the note does not claim a case and the existing glossary entry (acc., elided) was not rewritten. Kept.
- **333 πρυμνῇσι “at the sterns of the ships” against “the hindmost ships”**: kept; the Iliad table’s 11.600 row (ἐπὶ πρυμνῇ νηῒ “on the stern of the ship”, “on the hindmost ship” turned down) is the precedent. The note and gloss say the adjective is πρυμνός from πρύμνη.
- **351 / 357 ὀρόθυνε and ἔγειρε both “rouse”**: one English for two verbs five lines apart. Kept, because both tables fix them that way (ὀροθύνω “roused”, 10.332; ἐγείρω “rouse”); a note now tells them apart (see 357).
- **306 whole-line introduction**: the English is the Odyssey table’s (16.460, 17.74) with the name changed; it differs from iliad-033’s wording for the Tlepolemus line. The validator warns only on identical Greek, and the Odyssey row is the binding one. Kept, and new-renderings records the departure.
- **270 `i` “among the foremost” for μετὰ πρώτοισι**: not the table’s πρόμαχοι “foremost fighters” (that is 291), so there is no clash. Kept.
- **281 / 280 ἐρητύετ’ and ἧσθαι**: `l` “is held back” (present/gnomic) was kept; the gloss was repaired instead (see pass 2).
- **319 `l` “unless the son of Cronus himself should throw”**: ὅτε μή is “unless/except when” and the optative is of the unlikely event; no change.
- **Scansion**: the packet flags no line (“none”), so no line was scanned by hand and no sentence on irregularity was added. I did not rescan the other lines independently; the build’s scanner is the gate.
- **Quotation marks and neighbours**: four speeches (267–273, 275–294, 307–310, 312–327), each with “ on its first unit and ” on its last, and `mark` on the first unit of each; every other unit is inside a speech or narrative and carries no mark. The speech this part answers closes (”) at the end of iliad-079; the part ends in narrative (13.360), so nothing runs on into iliad-081. No change needed.
- **Known glossary entries left alone** (additions only): κιών is entered as “aor. part.” of κίω, but κιών is the present participle; ἐρητύετ’ now has a broadening for the present reading but the old imperfect reading stands. The old κιών entry is not part of this part’s gloss and was not rewritten; worth an owner decision if the glossary is ever revised.
- **Glosser’s other parses** (θωρήσσεσθον as 3 dual present, ἐλόωσι as a subjunctive with future sense, ἐτεύχετον as imperfect 3 dual, ὀρώρηται as perfect subjunctive): all agree with the line and the unit notes; no change.
